answer: An farming party who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the zenith history. Churn is counted in saffron, and wharf publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 21% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 340 account operation therefore ties up 29 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
